docs.title: EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW
PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - INTERVIEW RECORD
PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - INTERVIEW RECORD
PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - FIRST MEETING MINUTES
PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - SECOND MEETING MINUTES
PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES
PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a material volume report for a specified library.
raw_candidates.quote: report on the volume of material in a given library
raw_candidates.note: The summary explicitly identifies reporting material volume for a given library as a requirement.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report material volume for any point in time, including historical dates.
raw_candidates.quote: at any point in time
raw_candidates.note: The requirement calls for volume reporting beyond only the current moment.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall count all items associated with the selected library.
raw_candidates.quote: Counts all items with a location = your library
raw_candidates.note: The proposed report query specifies that items must be counted by library location.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the total number of items in the selected library.
raw_candidates.quote: Total items in library
raw_candidates.note: Total item volume is explicitly listed as a requested report breakdown.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of newly acquired items.
raw_candidates.quote: New acquisitions
raw_candidates.note: New acquisitions are explicitly included as a component of material volume.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of items currently on the shelf or checked in.
raw_candidates.quote: Items on the shelf (checked in)
raw_candidates.note: Checked-in shelf items are explicitly identified as a volume component.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of items currently out in circulation or checked out.
raw_candidates.quote: Items out in circulation (checked out)
raw_candidates.note: Checked-out items are explicitly identified as a volume component.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide separate counts for new acquisitions, checked-in items, and checked-out items in addition to the total.
raw_candidates.quote: all three counts separately plus a total
raw_candidates.note: The discussion explicitly requests separate component counts and an overall total.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow material volume to be broken down by category.
raw_candidates.quote: The report should allow breaking down volume in categories
raw_candidates.note: Category-based volume breakdown is stated as part of the Material Volume Report requirement.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of holds.
raw_candidates.quote: Number of holds
raw_candidates.note: Holds are explicitly listed as a required volume-report category.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of adult fiction items.
raw_candidates.quote: Number of adult fiction
raw_candidates.note: Adult fiction is explicitly listed as a required example category.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of board books.
raw_candidates.quote: Number of board books
raw_candidates.note: Board books are explicitly listed as a required example category.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support additional user-defined material categories.
raw_candidates.quote: Other customizable categories
raw_candidates.note: The summary requires categories beyond the listed examples to be customizable.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support category groupings such as fiction/non-fiction and format.
raw_candidates.quote: Groups by categories (fiction/non-fiction, format, etc.)
raw_candidates.note: These category dimensions are explicitly proposed for the report query.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the number of holds within each material category.
raw_candidates.quote: Shows breakdowns with holds count per category
raw_candidates.note: The proposed report specifically requires holds counts at the category level.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support filtering volume reports by acquisition date.
raw_candidates.quote: We can also add date filters
raw_candidates.note: Date filtering is proposed to enable time-based volume reporting.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report the volume of items acquired during selectable recent periods, including the last 30, 60, or 90 days.
raw_candidates.quote: how much volume has been added in the last 30/60/90 days
raw_candidates.note: The discussion explicitly requests acquisition-volume reporting for these time intervals.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support reporting volume changes over time.
raw_candidates.quote: build reports that show volume changes over time
raw_candidates.note: Volume-change reporting is explicitly stated as feasible and useful.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide branch managers with an overview of the capacity of all branches, not only their own branch.
raw_candidates.quote: I need to see the capacity of all branches in our system, not just my own.
raw_candidates.note: This is the central stated need for system-wide capacity visibility.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a high-level summary view showing all branches and their key capacity metrics simultaneously.
raw_candidates.quote: High-level overview of all branches' capacity at once
raw_candidates.note: The summary explicitly identifies an all-branch overview as a required interface capability.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to drill down from the overview into an individual branch's capacity details.
raw_candidates.quote: Ability to drill down into individual branches
raw_candidates.note: Drill-down is explicitly listed as part of the proposed interface.

raw_candidates.text: The system should visually indicate branch capacity status using color coding, such as green for under capacity, yellow for nearing capacity, and red for at or over capacity.
raw_candidates.quote: color-coding - green for under capacity, yellow for getting full, red for at/over capacity
raw_candidates.note: This is expressed as a proposed or tentative capability rather than a firm requirement.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to sort and filter branch capacity information by region, library type, and current load.
raw_candidates.quote: sort and filter. By region, by library type, by current load
raw_candidates.note: Sorting and filtering by these dimensions are explicitly requested and repeated in the summary.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support displaying and managing capacity information for the system's approximately 286 branch locations.
raw_candidates.quote: with 286 locations, the overview might get crowded
raw_candidates.note: The stated location count creates an interface scalability constraint, although the document does not define a specific presentation solution.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide capacity trend data indicating whether a branch's capacity or load is growing or shrinking over time.
raw_candidates.quote: Trend data (growth/shrink patterns)
raw_candidates.note: Trend visibility is requested to support long-term planning.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to export branch capacity information to CSV format.
raw_candidates.quote: Export to CSV
raw_candidates.note: CSV export is explicitly included in the discussion summary for users who need spreadsheet data.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall use a defined capacity metric or metrics for each branch, such as item count relative to shelf space, configured limits, or processing capacity.
raw_candidates.quote: what specific metrics define "capacity"?
raw_candidates.note: The document identifies the definition of capacity as an unresolved requirement that must be settled before implementation.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report, for each genre and format of material, the percentage of total circulations.
raw_candidates.quote: The percentage of total circulations
raw_candidates.note: This is an explicitly requested usage metric in the shelf space report.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report, for each genre and format of material, the percentage of the collection.
raw_candidates.quote: The percentage of the collection
raw_candidates.note: This is an explicitly requested collection-composition metric.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall report, for each genre and format of material, the percentage of total shelf space occupied.
raw_candidates.quote: The percentage of total shelf space
raw_candidates.note: This is an explicitly requested shelf-utilization metric.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide the shelf space report at the individual-library level.
raw_candidates.quote: The report should be available per library
raw_candidates.note: Branch managers need to review their local situation.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide the shelf space report at the system level.
raw_candidates.quote: The report should be available per library and per system.
raw_candidates.note: Users explicitly require an organization-wide view.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support comparing an individual library's results with the system average.
raw_candidates.quote: see how they compare to the system average
raw_candidates.note: The requested library and system views are intended to support comparison with system-wide results.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to filter shelf space utilization results by a specified date range.
raw_candidates.quote: Can we also filter by date range?
raw_candidates.note: Users need to compare periods such as Q1 and Q2 because seasonal collection usage matters.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a comparison view showing each library's genre-and-format breakdown side by side.
raw_candidates.quote: a "comparison" view that shows each library's breakdown side by side
raw_candidates.note: This view is requested to make library outliers easier to identify.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall count items by genre and format to calculate the percentage of the collection.
raw_candidates.quote: Count items per genre/format
raw_candidates.note: The data breakdown identifies item counts as the basis for the collection-percentage metric.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall sum checkouts by genre and format to calculate the percentage of circulations.
raw_candidates.quote: Sum checkouts per genre/format
raw_candidates.note: The data breakdown identifies checkout totals as the basis for the circulation-percentage metric.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall estimate shelf space by genre and format using item dimensions or an item-count proxy when direct shelf-space data is unavailable.
raw_candidates.quote: estimate based on item dimensions or use item count as a proxy
raw_candidates.note: Shelf space is not directly tracked, so the estimation method remains an implementation ambiguity.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches or locations.
raw_candidates.quote: a utility for transferring batches of items between branches
raw_candidates.note: This is the primary requested capability.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to query for candidate materials for transfer.
raw_candidates.quote: Query for candidate materials
raw_candidates.note: Candidate selection is a core step in the transfer workflow.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to save queries for repeated use.
raw_candidates.quote: Save queries for repeated use
raw_candidates.note: Users explicitly identify recurring transfers as requiring reusable queries.

raw_candidates.text: The system should allow authorized users to share saved queries with other users.
raw_candidates.quote: Save/share queries
raw_candidates.note: The technical design discussion expands saved queries to include sharing.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to manually select individual titles or items from query results.
raw_candidates.quote: Manually select titles from query results
raw_candidates.note: Users need to transfer only a subset of returned candidates.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall update the records of selected items to assign them to a new location.
raw_candidates.quote: Change records of selected items to new location
raw_candidates.note: Changing item records is required to execute the transfer.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support changing an item's location field as a transfer mechanism.
raw_candidates.quote: changing location field
raw_candidates.note: The requested location-field update is an explicit implementation mechanism.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall generate pull lists for items selected for transfer.
raw_candidates.quote: generating pull lists
raw_candidates.note: Pull lists are explicitly requested to support physically collecting items.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow transferred items to be reverted to their original locations after a specified period.
raw_candidates.quote: Revert items to original location after a set period of time
raw_candidates.note: Temporary transfers require scheduled return to the original location.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support automatic reversion of transferred items based on configurable criteria other than elapsed time.
raw_candidates.quote: revert "based on other criteria"
raw_candidates.note: Users request criteria-based reversion in addition to time-based reversion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support event-based automatic reversion when a transferred item's status changes to a configured status such as sold or returned.
raw_candidates.quote: when the item's status changes to "sold"
raw_candidates.note: Status changes are proposed as triggers for automatic reversion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support automatic reversion after a configurable number of days.
raw_candidates.quote: Revert after X days (date-based)
raw_candidates.note: A configurable elapsed-time trigger is explicitly requested.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support automatic reversion triggered when an item is checked out at the destination.
raw_candidates.quote: when item is checked out at the destination
raw_candidates.note: Destination checkout is identified as a requested event-based trigger.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall process large batch updates efficiently.
raw_candidates.quote: batch updates need to be efficient
raw_candidates.note: The document identifies performance as a constraint for installations with millions of items.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall process large transfers in smaller batches when necessary to avoid database locking.
raw_candidates.quote: process in smaller batches to avoid locking the database
raw_candidates.note: This is an explicit scalability and database-concurrency constraint.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall execute batch location updates with transaction safety.
raw_candidates.quote: Batch update of location field - straightforward database update with transaction safety.
raw_candidates.note: Transaction safety is identified as a required technical property of batch updates.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall log all item transfers for audit purposes.
raw_candidates.quote: Logging - track all transfers for audit purposes
raw_candidates.note: Auditable transfer records are explicitly required.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall restrict transfer functionality to authorized roles such as managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators.
raw_candidates.quote: limited to certain roles (managers, administrators, transfer coordinators)
raw_candidates.note: The document requires permission control because not all staff may transfer items.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall display a preview of the items and locations affected before applying a transfer.
raw_candidates.quote: the utility should show a preview before making changes
raw_candidates.note: Users need to review the proposed operation before records are changed.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall require confirmation before applying a previewed transfer.
raw_candidates.quote: Confirm?
raw_candidates.note: The example explicitly indicates that users should confirm the proposed changes.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide an undo function for item transfers.
raw_candidates.quote: we need an undo function
raw_candidates.note: Undo is requested to recover from accidental transfers.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall generate printable transit labels containing barcodes for transferred items.
raw_candidates.quote: generate transit labels
raw_candidates.note: Printable barcode labels are requested to support physical transit handling.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall notify designated users when an item transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.
raw_candidates.quote: If an item transfer is delayed or has issues, notify me.
raw_candidates.note: Transfer delay and problem alerts are explicitly requested.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall maintain transfer history for each item.
raw_candidates.quote: Can we track transfer history?
raw_candidates.note: Users need historical transfer data to identify items repeatedly assigned to unsuitable locations.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support transferring items to a temporary location for a specific event or program.
raw_candidates.quote: transfer items to a temporary location for a specific event or program
raw_candidates.note: The outreach use case requires temporary, event-associated transfers.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support reverting temporary event or program transfers after the associated event or program.
raw_candidates.quote: then revert them after the event
raw_candidates.note: Temporary event transfers explicitly require return after the event.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a report of missing and damaged items grouped by branch.
raw_candidates.quote: System provides reports of missing and damaged items per branch.
raw_candidates.note: This is explicitly identified as a required report for inventory auditing and collection management.

raw_candidates.text: The missing and damaged items report shall include item condition notes.
raw_candidates.quote: can the report include item condition notes?
raw_candidates.note: Condition details such as water damage or vandalism are requested to support root-cause analysis.

raw_candidates.text: The missing and damaged items report shall support filtering by date range.
raw_candidates.quote: The missing/damaged report can include date ranges
raw_candidates.note: Date-range reporting is requested for trend analysis, although the specific supported ranges are examples rather than a fixed list.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall generate a list of items that have been in transit longer than a configurable number of days.
raw_candidates.quote: items that have been in-transit for more than X days (X configurable)
raw_candidates.note: The requested report must identify delayed in-transit items using a configurable threshold.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a default in-transit threshold of 7 days.
raw_candidates.quote: probably 7 days default
raw_candidates.note: A seven-day default is proposed, but the wording indicates this value may require confirmation.

raw_candidates.text: The in-transit items report shall support reporting by branch.
raw_candidates.quote: per branch and per system
raw_candidates.note: Branch-level reporting is explicitly included in the clarified requirements.

raw_candidates.text: The in-transit items report shall support reporting for the entire library system.
raw_candidates.quote: per branch and per system
raw_candidates.note: System-wide reporting is explicitly included in the clarified requirements.

raw_candidates.text: The in-transit items report shall combine transit-to and transit-from items into a single report.
raw_candidates.quote: The report merges transit-to and transit-from into one report.
raw_candidates.note: Combining both transit directions is required to avoid requiring front-line staff to run separate reports.

raw_candidates.text: The in-transit items report shall support sorting by due date.
raw_candidates.quote: can we sort by due date?
raw_candidates.note: Sorting is requested so staff can prioritize chasing the oldest items first.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a utility and reports for identifying item records eligible for purging.
raw_candidates.quote: provide a utility and reports for identifying item records to purge
raw_candidates.note: The summary explicitly states the need for both a utility and reports to identify purge candidates.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to define customizable criteria for identifying items to purge.
raw_candidates.quote: based on customizable criteria
raw_candidates.note: Multiple participants require purge rules to be configurable rather than fixed.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support identifying items that have been in a specified status, such as missing, for longer than a user-defined duration.
raw_candidates.quote: An item has been in status "missing" for more than X months
raw_candidates.note: The requested criterion combines an item status with a configurable elapsed time.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support identifying items with a status of discard/weed as purge candidates.
raw_candidates.quote: An item has status "discard/weed"
raw_candidates.note: Discard/weed status is explicitly listed as a purge criterion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support identifying items that have not circulated for a user-defined period.
raw_candidates.quote: That haven't circulated in 5+ years
raw_candidates.note: Lack of circulation is explicitly requested as an activity-based purge criterion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support status-based purge criteria including missing, discard/weed, and damaged.
raw_candidates.quote: Status-based criteria (missing, discard/weed, damaged)
raw_candidates.note: The requested customizable criteria explicitly include these statuses.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support time-based purge criteria based on how long an item has been in a status.
raw_candidates.quote: Time-based criteria (in status for X months/years)
raw_candidates.note: The request explicitly identifies time in status as a configurable criterion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support activity-based purge criteria based on when an item last circulated.
raw_candidates.quote: Activity-based criteria (last circulated X days/months/years ago)
raw_candidates.note: The request explicitly identifies time since last circulation as a configurable criterion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall allow users to combine multiple purge criteria, including logical combinations such as AND.
raw_candidates.quote: The system should let us combine criteria.
raw_candidates.note: Users specifically request combining status, time, and circulation conditions.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a report to assist with converting items from one status to another.
raw_candidates.quote: Provide a report to assist in the conversion of items from one status to another
raw_candidates.note: The summary explicitly requires a status-conversion report.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support batch conversion of multiple items from one status to another.
raw_candidates.quote: changing 100 items from "missing" to "discard/weed" at once
raw_candidates.note: The example makes clear that status conversion must operate on many items at once.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a last-copy report identifying the last copies within a specified scope.
raw_candidates.quote: Provide a last copy report singling out a library system's last copies
raw_candidates.note: A last-copy report is identified as a critical collection-management need.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide last-copy reporting at the individual-library scope.
raw_candidates.quote: Sometimes we delete the last copy at our branch
raw_candidates.note: Users explicitly require a view that identifies the last copy held by a library or branch.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide last-copy reporting at the entire PINES system or consortium scope.
raw_candidates.quote: the last copy in the entire PINES system
raw_candidates.note: Users require protection against deleting the final consortium-level copy.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall determine whether each item is the only copy within the selected library or system scope and flag it when applicable.
raw_candidates.quote: is this the only copy in the specified scope (library or system)? If yes, flag it.
raw_candidates.note: The requested report behavior explicitly defines the copy-count check and flagging rule.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a quick and effective method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries.
raw_candidates.quote: deleting volume entries along with copy entries
raw_candidates.note: The summary explicitly requires coordinated deletion of volume and copy entries.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a method to delete records that have no items attached.
raw_candidates.quote: records with no items attached
raw_candidates.note: Deleting orphaned records is explicitly included in the requested cleanup functionality.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall present purge candidates through read-only reports before deletion.
raw_candidates.quote: Reports show candidates for purging (read-only)
raw_candidates.note: A read-only review stage is requested as a safety measure.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall require a separate confirmation step before performing actual deletions.
raw_candidates.quote: A separate confirmation step for actual deletions
raw_candidates.note: The requested confirmation step is intended to prevent accidental collection-wide deletion.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall maintain an audit trail for every purge, including who performed it, what was purged, and when.
raw_candidates.quote: track who purged what and when
raw_candidates.note: The requested audit trail must support accountability and troubleshooting.

raw_candidates.text: The system should support scheduling the purging utility to run automatically at a specified time, such as the end of each year.
raw_candidates.quote: can the purging utility be scheduled? Like, run automatically at the end of each year?
raw_candidates.note: Scheduling is raised as a desired capability, but the email does not establish whether it must be automated or manually approved.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall track deletion events for item, patron, bibliographic, and other record types.
raw_candidates.quote: What type of record was deleted (item/patron/bib)
raw_candidates.note: The emails explicitly require identifying the type of every deleted record.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall count record deletions.
raw_candidates.quote: We need to be able to count and track record deletions
raw_candidates.note: Counting deletions is stated as a distinct auditing need.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall associate each deletion event with the deleted record's identifier.
raw_candidates.quote: Fields: record_type, record_id, deleted_by, deleted_at, location
raw_candidates.note: The proposed audit-table fields explicitly include record_id.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall record the timestamp of each deletion.
raw_candidates.quote: When it was deleted
raw_candidates.note: A deletion timestamp is explicitly required for auditing and reporting.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall record the user who performed each deletion.
raw_candidates.quote: Who deleted it
raw_candidates.note: Identifying the deleting user is required for accountability.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall record the location or branch associated with the deletion or deleting user.
raw_candidates.quote: Where they were located (which branch)
raw_candidates.note: The requirement identifies the user's branch as a required audit attribute.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support reporting deletion counts by location.
raw_candidates.quote: count and track record deletions ... per location
raw_candidates.note: Location-based deletion reporting is explicitly requested.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall support reporting deletion counts by system.
raw_candidates.quote: The report should show deletions per location and per system.
raw_candidates.note: The document explicitly requires reporting deletions per system, although the meaning of system may need clarification.

raw_candidates.text: The system should record the status or reason associated with a deletion before the record is deleted.
raw_candidates.quote: Possibly why (status before deletion?)
raw_candidates.note: This is presented as a possible audit field, so whether it is mandatory remains ambiguous.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall persist deletion events in an audit table populated by a database deletion trigger.
raw_candidates.quote: A trigger in the database that logs deletions to an audit table
raw_candidates.note: The proposed implementation requires durable database-level logging rather than deletion data disappearing.

raw_candidates.text: The system shall provide a report interface for querying deletion audit records.

adjudicate_issues.detail: [adjudicator] Candidate C0007 ("Number of board books") is covered by existing requirements: REQ-001 (Material volume reporting) and REQ-002 (Material status counts). It should not be treated as uncovered or blacklisted; map it to REQ-001/REQ-002.

[adjudicator] Candidate C0220 ("can be queried by all transactions or by type of transaction") is covered by REQ-050 (Circulation transaction reporting) which requires counts by transaction type and collective counts. Map C0220 to REQ-050.

[adjudicator] Candidates C0378, C0379, C0380, C0381 (IntraPINES Loans reports by facility/system/all facilities/all systems) are covered by REQ-013 (Transit item reporting) which requires consolidated reports for items traveling to/from locations with branch and system scopes. Map these candidates to REQ-013.

[adjudicator] Candidate C0404 ("NonCat In House Use Count by Month") is covered by REQ-046 (Uncataloged inventory tracking) and REQ-050 (Circulation transaction reporting) which include counting/reporting of uncataloged activity. Map C0404 to REQ-046 / REQ-050.

[adjudicator] Candidate C0475 ("When their report was submitted") is covered by REQ-033 (Report execution queue) which requires showing submission time and status for queued reports. Map C0475 to REQ-033.

[adjudicator] The following uncovered candidates appear to represent legitimate, distinct system capabilities that are not represented by any current requirement and therefore should be added (or mapped to an expanded requirement): C0371 ("List of patrons who are BARRED" — a barred-patrons report), C0541 ("No hover tooltips for report titles" / hover-tooltips for report titles — a UI affordance), C0776 ("Transactions can be grouped by hour" — a time-bucketing/grouping dimension), and C0815 ("Program attendance tracking" — program attendance reports). Recommend that these be turned into explicit requirement…

[adjudicator] REQ-036 (Accessible user interfaces) and REQ-037 (Accessible HTML output) substantially overlap: REQ-036 mandates accessibility across interfaces and report features; REQ-037 mandates standards-compliant semantic HTML, alt text and ARIA for interfaces and report output. REQ-037 reads like a specific implementation detail of REQ-036. Recommend merging or making REQ-037 an explicit sub-requirement of REQ-036 to avoid duplication and potential inconsistent scope/wording.

[adjudicator] REQ-031 (Report output formats) and REQ-037 (Accessible HTML output) overlap for HTML report output. REQ-031 specifies export formats including HTML and requires standards-compliant HTML; REQ-037 specifies semantic HTML, alt text and ARIA labels. Clarify whether REQ-037 is the accessibility refinement of REQ-031's HTML requirement or whether REQ-031 must be extended to include the accessibility details to avoid separate possibly conflicting statements.

[adjudicator] Potential semantic conflict between REQ-036/REQ-037 (accessibility requirements that include ARIA and standards-compliant semantic HTML, alt text and accessible interfaces) and REQ-038 (Supported client platforms) which requires support for IE 6.0-or-later and Firefox 2.0-or-later. Those legacy browser baselines lack modern ARIA/HTML accessibility support, creating an operational conflict between delivering the stated accessibility features and supporting the specified legacy browser versions. Recommend resolving by (a) raising the minimum supported browser versions consistent with accessibil…

[adjudicator] Many consolidated requirements remain large and absorb many candidate refs (validation list). These requirements should be split for clarity and traceability. The following requirement ids were flagged as too broad in prior validation and should be decomposed into smaller, atomic requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005, REQ-007, REQ-013, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-026, REQ-028, REQ-031, REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-036, REQ-038, REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-044, REQ-050, REQ-051, REQ-053, REQ-055, REQ-058, REQ-060. Each should be examined and split so that each atomic capability maps…

[adjudicator] The original uncovered_candidates list included 13 entries reported as not covered by any requirement. Several of those are in fact covered (see coverage issues above). Update traceability mapping so that covered candidates (C0007, C0220, C0378, C0379, C0380, C0381, C0404, C0475) are associated with the requirements indicated above, and add new requirement entries for the remaining legitimate uncovered candidates (C0371, C0541, C0776, C0815) or incorporate them into appropriately split existing requirements.

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

Users shall be able to run reports immediately or schedule hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly execution. Scheduled results shall support configurable email recipients and recipient address books.

**Sources:**

- `D14` EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW — "No address book for report delivery"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "Ability to select Run ASAP, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly"
- `D20` PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY — "Email delivery of reports"

**Keywords:** reports, scheduling, email, recipients

### Area: report filtering

#### REQ-030: Report filtering

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

Users shall be able to filter reports using available fields and uploaded values. Text files containing barcodes or TCNs shall be usable as filter inputs, and survey names shall resolve to their internal identifiers.

**Sources:**

- `D14` EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW — "No ability to upload text files for filtering"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "upload a text file such as barcodes or TCN to use for filtering on a report"
- `D19` PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES — "requires the system to resolve names to IDs internally"
- `D20` PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY — "Can't filter by some fields that should be available"

**Keywords:** reports, filters, barcodes, tcns, surveys

### Area: report output

#### REQ-031: Report output formats

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

The system shall export report results in CSV, Excel, and HTML formats. HTML shall be standards-compliant, and exports shall preserve record structure without introducing duplicate rows.

**Sources:**

- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "Output would be in Excel, HTML, and CSV format"
- `D19` PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES — "Excel, HTML, and CSV formats are required"
- `D20` PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY — "export to Excel but the data has too many duplicate rows"
- `D14` EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW — "Provide multiple output formats and scheduling options"

**Keywords:** csv, excel, html, exports

### Area: report processing

#### REQ-033: Report execution queue

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

The system shall execute long-running reports as background jobs in a managed queue. Users shall see queue position, submission time, status, completion or failure, and shall be able to cancel scheduled or running reports and prioritize important report types.

**Sources:**

- `D12` Report features and interface requirements — "A director's board report should be able to jump ahead of a staff member's ad-hoc query."
- `D19` PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES — "cancel a scheduled or running report"
- `D14` EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW — "No background processing for long-running reports"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "Staff should be able to see where their report is in the queue"
- `D18` PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - SECOND MEETING MINUTES — "Report queue visibility is important"
- `D20` PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY — "Ability to see where your report is in the queue."

**Keywords:** reports, queue, background, cancellation, status

### Area: report results

#### REQ-032: Report result context

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

Report results shall include the query selections, date criteria, null values, and blank fields used or returned by the report. This context shall allow users to interpret and reproduce the result set.

**Sources:**

- `D12` Report features and interface requirements — "System provides query selections along with results."
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results"
- `D19` PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES — "All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results"
- `D14` EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW — "All nulls and blank fields included in results"
- `D20` PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY — "All nulls and blank fields must be included in results"

**Keywords:** reports, criteria, nulls, traceability

### Area: report security

#### REQ-029: Report safeguards

**Priority:** P1 — Must have - critical for core operation, legal/audit compliance, or data integrity; blocking for the first release.

Report template changes shall not compromise result accuracy or expose excluded records. The system shall prevent unauthorized changes that would display deleted items or alter protected selection and display rules.

**Sources:**

- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "they should not be able to alter the template to display deleted items"
- `D12` Report features and interface requirements — "can't alter the template to display deleted items."
- `D11` Re: Financial reporting requirements - discussion thread — "System can generate a report of the value of items (based on data in item record)"

**Keywords:** reports, accuracy, safeguards, deleted records

### Area: reporting

#### REQ-059: Staff and operational reports

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

The system shall provide predefined operational, analytical, financial, board, executive, inventory, capacity, demographic, transit, shelf-space, weeding, and staff productivity reports. Reports shall support consortium-wide and participating-library scopes.

**Sources:**

- `D18` PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - SECOND MEETING MINUTES — "Board/executive reports need to be pre-defined"
- `D20` PINES STAFF REPORTS SURVEY - RESULTS SUMMARY — "Staff productivity reports (time spent per transaction)"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "basic statistics like those required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid"
- `D12` Report features and interface requirements — "Pre-defined reports for library boards"

**Keywords:** reports, executive, inventory, operations, staff

### Area: system integration

#### REQ-044: Enterprise ILS integration

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

Management processes shall operate with the enterprise ILS data structures and Acquisitions and Cataloging functionality. The system shall support multiple library locations, interact with the OPAC without constraining it, and exchange vendor data through APIs and standard files.

**Sources:**

- `D18` PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - SECOND MEETING MINUTES — "rely on the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging modules"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "rely on the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System"
- `D19` PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES — "Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System"

**Keywords:** ils, opac, vendors, integration

### Area: uncataloged materials

#### REQ-046: Uncataloged inventory tracking

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

The system shall track uncataloged materials as inventory even without complete catalog records. Inventory records shall support counting, circulation reporting, and identification of how materials are used.

**Sources:**

- `D15` PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - INTERVIEW RECORD — "track these as inventory even though they're not fully cataloged"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "Ability to control inventory of uncataloged material"
- `D17` PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - FIRST MEETING MINUTES — "Tracking and verifying financial transactions"

**Keywords:** uncataloged, inventory, circulation, tracking

#### REQ-047: Uncataloged material processing

**Priority:** P2 — Should have - important for the daily workflows of key stakeholders; implement in the first release if feasible.

The system shall support rapid distribution and processing of uncataloged materials while minimizing branch labor. Workflows shall support high-volume handling and quick distribution.

**Sources:**

- `D15` PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - INTERVIEW RECORD — "quick distribution (we need to process these fast)"
- `D10` DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION — "Minimal branch labor"

**Keywords:** uncataloged, processing, distribution, labor
